title: Preparation of Thermoresponsive Nanostructured Surfaces for Tissue Engineering
protocol: Dissolve styrene, ECT, and ACVA in 40 ml of 1,4-dioxane.
Freeze the solution in liquid nitrogen under vacuum for 15-20 min.
Thaw the solution gradually at room temperature (RT).
Repeat the freeze-pump-thaw degassing cycle three times to remove reactive species.
Polymerize at 70 °C for 15 hr in an oil bath to obtain polystyrene (PSt) with a molecular weight of 13,500.
Precipitate PSt macro RAFT agent with 800 ml of ether and dry in vacuo.
Dissolve IPAAm monomer, PSt macro RAFT agent, and ACVA in 4 ml of 1,4-dioxane.
Remove the oxygen in the solution by performing freeze-pump-thaw degassing cycles.
Perform a polymerization at 70 °C for 15 hr in an oil bath after degassing to obtain synthesized St-IPAAm with a molecular weight of 32,800.
Wash glass substrates (24 mm x 50 mm) with acetone and ethanol.
Sonicate the washed substrates for 5 min to remove surface contaminants.
Dry the substrates in an oven at 65 °C for 30 min.
Activate the surfaces of the substrates using oxygen plasma (400 W, 3 min).
Immerse the substrates in toluene containing 1% hexyltrimethoxysilane overnight at room temperature.
Wash the silanized substrates in toluene and immerse in acetone for 30 min to remove unreacted agents.
Anneal substrates for 2 hr at 110 °C to thoroughly immobilize the surface.
Cut the silanized substrates by a glass cutter to 25 mm x 24 mm to fit the cell culture dishes (dish size: φ35 mm).
Place the Langmuir film instrument in a cabinet to prevent the accumulation of dust.
Wash the Langmuir trough and barriers with distilled water and ethanol to remove contaminants.
Dry the trough and barriers by wiping with a lintless towel.
Fill the trough with approximately 110 ml of distilled water.
Set the barriers on both sides of the trough.
Heat a platinum Wilhelmy plate until it turns red and then wash with distilled water to remove contaminants.
Suspend the Wilhelmy plate on a wire attached to the surface-pressure-measurement instrument.
Zero the surface-pressure-measurement instrument according to manufacturer's protocol.
Compress the air-water interface on the trough by the barriers until the interface reaches approximately 50 cm² without any drops of polymer.
Aspirate small contaminants until the surface pressure is nearly 0 mN/m.
Reposition the barriers on both sides.
Add distilled water to compensate for the decrease of distilled water from step 3.6.
Dissolve 5 mg of synthesized St-IPAAm molecule in 5 ml of chloroform.
Gently drop 27 µl of St-IPAAm dissolved in chloroform onto the trough using a microsyringe or micropipette.
Wait for 5 min to allow complete evaporation of chloroform.
Move both barriers horizontally to compress the St-IPAAm molecule at the interface.
Maintain compression rate of the barriers at 0.5 mm/sec until the target area of 50 cm2 is reached.
Measure the surface pressure (π)-Am isotherms with the platinum Wilhelmy plate attached to the surface-pressure-measurement instrument during compression according to manufacturer's protocol.
Maintain the compressed surface for 5 min to allow the St-IPAAm molecules to relax.
Transfer the Langmuir film to a hydrophobically modified glass substrate using a transfer apparatus for 5 min.
Fix the hydrophobic glass substrate in parallel on the device.
Connect the device to an alignment stage.
Move perpendicularly.
Culture bovine carotid artery endothelial cells (BAECs) to one third confluence at 37 °C in 5% CO2 and 95% air on tissue culture polystyrene (TCPS).
Treat BAECs with 3 ml of 0.25% trypsin-EDTA for 3 min at 37 °C in 5% CO2 and 95% air.
Deactivate the trypsin-EDTA by adding 10 ml of DMEM containing 10% FBS.
Collect the cell suspension to a 50 ml conical tube.
Centrifuge the cells at 120 x g for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant from the centrifuged cells.
Resuspend the cells with 10 ml of DMEM.
Place St-IPAAm surfaces under ultraviolet light on a clean bench for sterilizing for 5 min.
Seed recovered cells on the St-IPAAm surfaces at a concentration of 1.0 x 10^4 cells/cm^2.
Observe the seeded cells on the surfaces by a microscope equipped with an incubator at 37 °C in 5% CO2 and 95% air.
Record time-lapse images of adherent BAECs for approximately 24.5 hours at 37°C using a phase-contrast microscope with 10X magnification.
After BAEC adhesion, record detachment of the BAECs from the St-IPAAm surface at 20°C for approximately 3.5 hours.
Culture BAECs in the same manner described in Section 4.
Seed a total of 1.0 x 10^5 cells/cm^2 on St-IPAAm surfaces.
Incubate seeded BAECs for 3 days at 37°C in 5% CO2.
Confluent BAECs spontaneously detach at 20°C.
